One of Star Trek's most iconic fight scenes was also one of the most miserable to film. William Shatner recently talked about how bad it was to do the Gorn fight in the original series, and how it felt even worse to actually shoot than it looked onscreen.

"Arena" is likely one of the most memorable episodes of Star Trek decades later. Unfortunately, that's not necessarily a great thing, as it contains (in my opinion) an obscenely bad fight scene. It's one in which Shatner's Kirk fights in slow motion with a member of the Gorn species. In addition to the iconic scene aging poorly, with effects that even looked dated back then, Shatner mentioned at New York Comic Con it was also terrible to film (via Reddit):

The guy was in this rubber suit; it's 120 degrees in the desert. I have to roll in the regolith and get all dusty. And when you go to brush it off, you get blood.

The "regolith," which by the way are the minerals that settle on top of bedrock, were so abrasive that it made the fight very difficult to film. I'm sure most Star Trek fans don't need to rewatch the scene with a Paramount+ subscription to know the end result ultimately wasn't worth the pain and toil. Still, lame fight aside, "Arena" is a pretty compelling episode.

I Just Found Out Wil Wheaton Apologized To Patrick Stewart After TNG, But I'm Not Surprised By The Captain's Response

"Arena" starts when Kirk and the Gorn are transported to the planet to battle thanks to a third species named the Metrons. The Metrons wish to see a fight to the death, but are impressed when Kirk outmaneuvers the Gorn and spares its life instead. Both are then returned to their ship, with the lesson being that brains can overcome brawn with some quick thinking and skills.

It's great to hear William Shatner talk about the sillier times, as Star Trek fans were hit with some heavy news as of late. The passing of Walter Koenig was a gut punch to many, and following it with Patrick Stewart's death had many Trekkies out of the count. Shatner has even joked he's keeping an eye out for the Grim Reaper, trying to take the edge off such a heavy time.

As for Star Trek in general, there's an overarching question about what direction the franchise is headed after its 60th anniversary. There's a movie in development, but with no solid timeline and no word that there are any shows actively being made, there are a lot of questions that still need to be answered.

For the time being, there's a lot of Star Trek to watch and enjoy over on Paramount+. Those who have never seen "Arena can go and check it out now for the first time, or some of the other classic Trek shows as we wait for new entries in the franchise.

#3529. 12 Best Video Game Stocking Stuffers Under $30 That People Actually Want

Ugh. It’s my least-favorite time of year: Black Friday season. I hate this overwhelming capitalist-ass shopping holiday for many reasons, but one of my more petty pet peeves is the big push for the blandest, most cringey “gamer”-themed gifts ever at mainstream shopping destinations. I’m talking like, this “Smells like video game rage” candle, neon lights and blankets that say stuff like, “Can’t hear you, I’m gaming,” or the classic “I paused my game to be here” T-shirt. Crap that really leans into the awful “gamer” stereotype and that, for many of us, is embarrassing to receive from a relative who knows, like, one fact about us, which is that we are into video games.

If you’ve arrived at this article and have been guilty of giving such gifts before, please absolve yourself. The internet does not make this easy. Gaming gift guides are full of this junk, and if you’re not into games yourself, finding decent stuff for someone who likes them can be really annoying and challenging, especially on a budget. Most gamers probably have a lot of the tech and games they want already, and knowing what people have and what they might like can be extremely challenging if you don’t have an easy way to look at their Steam libraries.

So I’m here to give you a hand with 12 ideas for stocking stuffer gifts (read: will reasonably fit in a normal-sized Christmas stocking) under $30 that will probably be relevant to folks who like playing video games on the regular. These are all things that most people will be at least mildly pleased to receive and will probably use as long as you put in the bare minimum amount of thought to make sure you’re not getting Switch accessories for someone who doesn’t have a Switch or something.

Good controllers are so dang expensive and cheap ones are usually garbage, but the 8BitDo controllers are both of solid quality and inexpensive. These pleasant wireless controllers come in several cute pastel colors, are usable for PC gaming (or Android, I guess), and are quite inexpensive for as good as they are. Normally $29.99 on Amazon, as I write this they’re on sale for $22.99.

If you’ve got an Xbox gamer in the house, this charging stand works with all Xbox Series, One, and Elite Series 1 Wireless controllers, which your giftee almost certainly has at least one of. It’s normally $49.99, but Amazon has a Black Friday deal going that brings it all the way down to $18.99, so you may want to jump on it soon.

The Nintendo Switch 2 came out a year and a half ago, and with it came what’s effectively webcam support. However, my experience is that not a lot of people are using this feature, not because it’s a bad idea necessarily, but because they don’t want to buy the expensive bespoke webcam Nintendo is selling and don’t want to move the normal one they have on their PC over to their Switch every time. So right now, for $24.98 on Amazon ($34.99 normally) you can grab a Hori USB camera that’s licensed by Nintendo and works with the Switch 2. Actually having this set up with the Switch 2 will probably prompt more people to actually bust it out (it would certainly work on me).

If your gamer likes to sit at a desk, grab ’em a mug warmer like this Sweetfull option that’s currently $16.99, down from $19.99. It’s exactly what it sounds like, keeping the liquid warm. Great for tea, coffee, and hot cocoa drinkers who have told their families to stop buying them tea/coffee/cocoa every year because they now have too much.

It’s a little cliche, but I don’t know anyone who doesn’t think a light bar is at least a little cool. This one is inexpensive ($11.99 right now, down from $14.99), simple, and looks nice, though it’ll probably stick out of the top of the stocking a bit and give away your game.

Great for PC gamers. Comes in several colors and is $8 max when not on sale. Sounds lame, but is actually very useful. The sort of thing no one buys for themselves but is always grateful to get.

Check first, but an awful lot of people who are into video games pair that interest with a card-collecting hobby. PokÃ©mon cards are a nightmare to get nowadays, but if you can snag a pack or two from the 30th Celebration set, most PokÃ©mon card fans will be happy. Magic: The Gathering‘s Reality Fracture set is a good, safe bet for Magic fans, and the One Piece TCG is currently on a set called The Dominance of God.

Zojirushi is a great brand that makes a lot of great things, including water bottles. These are usually more expensive, but for Black Friday this blue one is down to $23.49 (other colors are also on sale under $30; I cover mine with stickers which you can do to give yours a personal touch). These things are durable and can support hot or cold bevvies, and from personal experience I can say it keeps cold water cold for hours. It’s easy to forget to drink water while engrossed in a really good game, and this bottle serves as a good reminder.

There are aÂ tonÂ of really cool, low-cost stickers, skins, and cases out there with which to protect one’s Nintendo Switch, and chances are your gamer wants one, because unless they have a sick special-edition Switch, those things are very bland aesthetically. Loads of them are under $30 and they come in all sorts of colors and styles. Just make sure you’re confident in which Switch (original or Switch 2) they have, so you get them one that fits.

This is another one of those items that I’d never go out of my way to buy for myself, but which I’d be grateful to receive and would absolutely give a whirl. Again, check and make sure you’re getting grips for the correct controller first: these work on Xbox or PlayStation.

Seriously. I don’t recommend gift cards as a singular gift for someone you care deeply about unless they ask for it explicitly, as it can come off as a bit thoughtless. But as one of several small items in a stocking for a younger relative or fellow adult you’re close to, this is a great additive option. A Steam gift card will go over well with almost anyone who plays games on their PC because they can buy whatever game has been on their wishlist without you having to guess at it. V-bucks are a great option if you know the person plays Fortnite. You can also get cards for the digital storefronts on PlayStation,Â Xbox, or Nintendo consoles. All of these will be welcome for anyone who uses these services.

#3528. From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding

The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was said to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

In 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately said yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

Like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

Designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

Princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

As Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”

Princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, said to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

All royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

The wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages

There were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

Together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.)

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

On the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

Although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

Over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

#3527. Apple has three products coming next year that I’m very excited for

Apple is wrapping up a packed year for new products, but there are already several 2027 launches I’m very excited for. Here are my current most anticipated new products rumored for next year.

The iPhone’s 20th anniversary is rumored to bring a special new model that’s been dubbed ‘iPhone 20 Pro.’

iPhone 20 Pro is expected to introduce a new design inspired by the iPhone Air, reintroducing curves and possibly titanium, and with a quad-curved display that wraps around the edges for a bezel-free appearance.

I recently decided the iPhone Duo wasn’t the right model for me. While I’ll certainly be interested to see how the device evolves in its second generation, I’m far more excited for the iPhone 20 Pro as a fresh iteration on slab phones. Combining the strengths of a Pro model (cameras, battery) with the design traits of iPhone Air sounds very compelling.

I’ve been using Apple’s HomeView a lot since getting one earlier this month. And despite some Siri hiccups likely tied to the iOS 27.3 beta, I’m overall really loving the product and my family is too.

Because HomeView has been a hit for us, I’m eager to see how Apple evolves and expands it with the rumored ‘HomeView Ultra’ with a 9-inch screen that can automatically rotate 360° to face whoever’s speaking.

I have no complaints about the current HomeView’s size, but am intrigued by a larger screen’s impact on the overall experience. Mostly though, the idea of a HomeView that automatically rotates to face you sounds really useful. There’s a spot in my kitchen that would be perfect for kitchen and dining room use if the screen could swivel automatically.

The Apple Watch Series 13 might introduce an overhauled design, with one leaker claiming it will break compatibility of watch bands.

I’m tempering my expectations for this, since plenty of Apple Watch redesign rumors have come and gone with little actual change. But Mark Gurman has hinted we might get a redesigned Watch next year too. And after years of the same basic look, I’m fascinated to see what the next generation of Apple Watch design could be.

I’m very happy with my Apple Watch Series 12, and it’s becoming even more powerful with watchOS 27.3. But it’s very much an update focused on internals, so if Apple does deliver an external overhaul, the new Watch will merit its spot among my most anticipated products list.

Which new Apple products are you most hoping for or anticipating for 2027? Let us know in the comments.

It’s hard to believe The Late Show with Stephen Colbert has been off of the air for half a year now. It’s presence was so undeniable for so long, sometimes I still feel like it’s around even though it’s definitely cancelled. Stephen Colbert’s kept busy, of course. He’s writing an LOTR movie (though we’ll have to see how it pans out after that merger)! Now that he does have more downtime he’s said there’s something his wife wants him to get into.

TV hours in general are known for being grueling, and late night is its own beast when it comes to hours worked. Despite the word “late” in the title, Colbert’s show actually shot in New York during the day, but putting on five shows a week is not for the faint of heart. I’m not saying Colbert used to be an avid exerciser before taking on the CBS gig (who knows?), but from the sounds of things, working on she show didn’t help. He’s not getting any younger, either, and now his late night stint is over, he wants to make some lifestyle changes.

Exercising. I think my wife has waited long enough. It’s time for abs. I want to be swole. You’re not even going to recognize me. I’m going to be ripped. You’re going to be able to bounce a quarter off my ass and get back two dimes and a nickel. Brace yourself. It’s finally happening.

The man was taking a slew of questions from his fellow late night hosts in a profile with THR when he admitted to wanting to get fit, fit, fit. The only time I’ve ever seen Stephen Colbert really attempt anything related to fitness was like eight years ago when The Late Show did an interview with the late Ruth Bader Ginsberg that included mobility stretches and some minor lifting, oh and one shot of Stephen Colbert pulling up his shirt and exposing his all-time dad bod.

I can hardly blame the former late night host for not making the time for exercise. We learned a few months ago his writing team was working long hours and making monologue changes on the fly in order to stay ahead of social media during their later filming days. The thanks they got was getting fired and having just a few days to exit the studio. His stuff was shipped off to a museum. He went to his brother’s wedding, and then moved on. The one upside is now he has all the time in the world to get into shape.

So far, we haven’t seen Stephen Colbert become a fitness influencer in the days since The Late Show ended. However, there’s always time, and I will certainly be keeping my eyes peeled the next time the former late night host makes an appearance. Is that arm definition? Is there any hint of abs? Only time will tell.

#3525. Who Will Be The Next Bond Girl?

Since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, new Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

The exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). Her magnetic performance made Madeleine an unforgettable Bond girl, especially since her character plays a decisive role in the arc of Craig’s character: at the end of No Time to Die, the famous spy sacrifices himself to save her and their daughter, Mathilde. For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

In a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she said with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”

When pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux said. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”

The online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

Bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”

Denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”

#3524. 12 Astonishing Indie Games To Buy Or Wishlist This Thanksgiving Day

It’s Thanksgiving! The annual pause from the incessant thankstaking that otherwise consumes us all, and as is traditional all around the world, we remember the day Earth was recaptured from the Xix Muthra Horde through the celebration of indie gaming. In a ceremony that goes as far back as 2022, we’ve picked out a pile of lesser-known indie games that we can stuff on our Steam wishlists with mad abandon.

Whoever named this “Thanksgaming,” however, has a lot to answer for. It doesn’t even work as a pun, let alone communicate that this is a collection of unknown indie games submitted to Kotaku by email, and then somewhat randomly selected and featured on the site. It’s all about offering you an eclectic range of fabulous-looking games that you can add to your wishlist, or buy and play right now, that you’d otherwise not likely see on a major gaming website. So dive in! If nothing here takes your interest, then your interest is poorly calibrated. You should get that checked.

Developer: SoÃ­n, Talbone Release Date: TBA Steam, Itch

Drifting meets rhythm gaming in this space-based taxi sim. That was a fun sentence to type out, because I don’t think there’s any other job in which you’d get to do it. It’s about racing around the solar system to underground Brazilian DJ beats, all with the goal of paying an “infinite debt.” And, well, watch the trailer! It’s amazing! Look at that astonishing art, and listen to what I’m going to pretend I already knew was Baile Funk. There’s a demo on Steam.

Developer: Victor Vergara, Alex Vergara Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

While an obvious nod to Geometry Wars,Â Geometry Rift appears to be a lot more than an homage to Bizarre Creations’ bizarre creation. This bullet hell roguelite blends the arcade classic withÂ Vampire Survivors elements, to create a full-frontal assault on your eyes. The nice kind, though. I mean, it looks beautiful, and I very much want to be playing it. Which I can, via the demo on Steam! This is being created by a father and son team from Spain, and was nominated for inclusion here by a third-party who just wants to see it getting more attention.

Developer: Lunheim Studios Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

At long bloody last someone’s finally combined pachinko and dungeon crawling. I was beginning to get annoyed.Â Peglin opened the door, andÂ Bumpers and Dragons has stepped through it. It’sÂ PeggleÂ as violence, where your bumpers are weapons, bought, upgraded and arranged on the board as you see fit, in a roguelite with a procedurally created set of dungeons and permanent progression.

Developer: Longhand Electric Release Date: Out now Steam

I loves me any game that lets me step inside paintings, whether it’sÂ Mario or this intriguing-looking free game.Â The Stone Ship came out in July, but completely passed me by (I’m installing it as I type). It’s a first-person game where paintings, photographs and maps come to life as you shift into their depicted scenes, scored by a gorgeous violin soundtrack composed and performed by Caroline Karpinska. ApparentlyÂ The Stone Ship was originally intended to be a chapter from a 2025 game,Â Overlook Trail (which also looks amazing!), but grew into its own standalone entity.

Developer: Jeffrey Nordin Release Date: Out now Steam

Released a couple of weeks ago, but yet to get attention, is the stunningly-namedÂ The House Dreams Along With Them, a first-person puzzle game in which you bring dreams into reality while exploring a modern-looking home. It’s about discovering the “reification of night,” which is a phrase that has brought me a great deal of pleasure. Inspired byÂ Myst (pwt-ooey),Â The Room and escape rooms, it looks splendidly bizarre. There’s a demo on Steam.

Developer: AstronautCat Studios Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

This trailer properly spooked me! It’s superbly well put together, compiled from the found footage of a missing cinema employee.Â Late Shift is about exploring and spotting anomalies in a looping reality that evokes Backrooms-like creepypastas, but showing clear and welcome influences from Control as well. Its mix of art styles, impossible architecture and jumpy nature feel really evocative to me. Can’t wait.

Developer: TMA Games Release Date: Out now (Early Access) Steam

Torment Hexus had me at “kicking CEOs out of windows.” It also had me at combining match-3 spellcasting alongside a tactical roguelite combat grid. What I’m communicating is that it has me. Now, at least: this entered Early Access in August this year, and intends to emerge fully-formed by some point in 2027. It’s currently playable, “pretty smooth and polished,” they say, but there are plans to add many more bosses, new spells, and a big ol’ story to justify multiple runs through the intriguing concept.

Developer: Mullet Games Release Date: 2027 Steam

Building a city in the desert is hard enough, what with the lack of water and basic resources, but what about the massive sandstorms blowing in and burying your settlement in sand? That’s the setup forÂ Storm Settlers (a name I struggle to see how Ubisoft will allow, given the genre overlap with itsÂ Settlers franchise), a super-cute and challenging city-builder. To survive your little guys will have to dig down in the hope of discovering the water table, while also building up defenses against the ceaseless storms that sweep over your town. The game is having a public playtest in December.

Developer: Pixelnest Studio Release Date: Q1 2027 Steam

One of my favorite phenomenon is watching as rudimentary gaming genres cross over and develop complexity, as if driven by the same forces that cause evolution to keep pointing things toward becoming crabs.Â Cosmo Cargo is a great example of this, merging the trend for inventory management games with the trend for auto-battlers, and creating a space-exploration game with hireable crews, hostile enemies, and battles based on the synergies created by the way you’ve combined cargo in your inventory. There’s a demo, of course, and the game is out next year.

Developer: ElSchorscho Release Date: December 2 Steam

I have a real soft spot for the dumbest incremental games, with their moreish progression and self-effacing inherent nonsense, and Drunk Woodcutter perfectly fits that bill. Due out next week, the short game is about chopping logs with increasingly silly tools…while getting drunk. This leads to hacking at logs with a banjo, and making money in the process, and as such reflects all our lives.

Developer: Lost Token Release Date: Out now Steam

Theropods is a traditional point-and-click adventure, but with the twist of containing no words or dialog at all. You play as a young cave women living with a tribe, haunted by dreams of the gruesome death of her mother in the mouth of a dinosaur. Yup, it’s a dinos and cavemen living together story! TakeÂ that, evolution. Now an adult, she needs to get on with the caveperson life, be it hunting, mending pots, or saving her people from the terrifying attack of marauding enemies, raging fires, and alien artifacts falling from the sky. Doing this with no words at all makes for a simpler game, but an intriguing one, boosted by some utterly stunning old-school pixel art animations.

Developer: Speldosa Interactive Release Date: Dec 7 Steam

A third-person platformer crossed withÂ PowerWash?! Yes please! That’sÂ Muri: Wildwoods where you play as an adorable mousey cleaning up and restoring an island to make it all lovely. To get around, it’s third-person jumping and climbing, and there are even watergun-based puzzles to solve. Powerwashing with double-jump is something I didn’t know I needed, but now it’s all-consuming. Thankfully there’s only a couple of weeks to wait until it’s out!

Thanksgiving is officially upon us, and many TV and movie fans are going to be re-watching their favorite festive programming. Whether its Friends' Thanksgiving episodes or a trip to Star's Hallow from Gilmore Girls, there's plenty to chose from. Unfortunately we got some bad news for TV addicts, specifically those with a Netflix subscription. Namely that the streaming platform has cancelled two more shows after just one season, and they both star big celebrities.

Netflix has a reputation for cancelling shows too soon, and it's not going to shake those allegations anytime soon. Deadline is reporting that the streamer recently dropped Will Ferrell's comedy The Hawk. That's not the only victim, as Netflix has also cancelled Dutch drama Amsterdam Empire, starring Famke Janssen. Fans of those shows are likely starting the Thanksgiving holiday with some disappointment about them not returning for sophomore seasons.

Perhaps this shouldn't be all that surprising. After all, The Hawk suffered from poor reviews upon its release back in July. Still, the show featured some stellar comedic talent, with Will Ferrell joined by legends like Molly Shannon, Fortune Feimster and Chris Parnell. The title role Lonnie "Hawk" Hawkins didn't go down as one of the best Will Ferrell characters, but there were folks who watched the silly golf comedy.

Then there's Amsterdam Empire, which had arguably less hype around it than Ferrell's comedy series. Starring Famke Janssen (Goldeneye, The X-Men movies), the show followed her character Betty Jonkers, a former pop star whose coffee-mogul husband is hiding some shady dealings. The show was shot entirely in Dutch, which is the accomplished actress' first language. Unfortunately the show is now over after just one season, which ended on an exciting cliffhanger. This comes after Janssen was noticeably left out of Avengers: Doomsday, despite so many of her X-Men co-stars reprising their roles in the upcoming Marvel movie.

These two titles join the ranks of many shows that Netflix has dropped way too early, to dismay of fans. Some other titles to have suffered this fate include The OA, which was cancelled after two wild seasons and a huge cliffhanger. Then there was Sense8, which got cancelled but eventually got a movie finale after fans made their voices known. Fans have also been hoping to see more of David Fincher's Mindhunter since the last episode aired back in 2019.

Only time will tell how fans of The Hawk and Amsterdam Empire respond to these two shows being cut off at the knees so early in their life on Netflix. For now, the two shows are currently streaming in their entirety as part of the 2026 movie release list. We'll have to see if Will Ferrell and/or Famke Janssen end up responding to this news, especially since it comes in the midst of the Thanksgiving holiday.

#3521. The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace’s ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Press Tour Looks

Before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the new Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and said, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to New York." She said, "No, absolutely not."

Right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in New York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

My personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Mckenna is a big fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

She's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

What she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

Mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

He said, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she said, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

She was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR said, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

It makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

The way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had said that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”

But we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I said, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie."

What was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie."

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me new references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

What made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

That was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

With the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom said, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a big franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has said, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a big fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

What do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

I think the big movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

The looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How important is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

It kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?"

I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

What is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

It's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”

Every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most important part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. Mckenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

Will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

In a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the New York City premiere?

We are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

In the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Pamella then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

So when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and said, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it."

What's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend said, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it."

#3519. Jim Curtis Shares Rare Post About ‘Love’ for His Girlfriend Jennifer Aniston

Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, is expressing his affection for the Friends star in a rare public message.

Taking to his Instagram Stories on Wednesday, November 25, Curtis, 50, shared a picture of a cafe with the punny message written on its windows. The window text read, “I love you so matcha.”

While sharing the snap to his social media, Curtis left no doubt who was on his mind while reading those words, with the hypnotherapist tagging Aniston, 57, directly underneath.

The Instagram post comes several months after Curtis admitted that he was forced to adjust to a new level of fame after striking up a romance with the Horrible Bosses star.

“To be quite honest, that was something to get used to because I’ve been pretty public for a long time but never this level or this, kind of, segment,” Curtis said on the September 8 episode of “The Jamie Kern Lima Show” about making headlines with his and Aniston’s romance.

He continued, “I’ve never been in the Hollywood kind of trades, the press. No one has really cared who I’ve dated in the past. So that was an adjustment for me, but it was a real learning experience, too.”

Curtis noted that he learned to block out the chatter about his personal life, adding that he wants to focus on his work and helping people. According to Curtis, this is what “matters most.”

“Don’t Google yourself again, Jim, to see what the news is saying today. And that took like, you know, three or four months. And now, the kind of thing if a tree falls in the woods and no one is there to hear it, doesn’t make a noise,” he said. “I told my family, like, ‘You don’t need to send me the latest shot of me on a boat with my stomach hanging out’ type of thing. These are just private moments any couple have and [fame] just kind of highlighted.”

The couple have been linked since 2025 after meeting through mutual friends before their romance grew organically.

“We found out that we had mutual friends, and we started to just chat,” Curtis said on a January episode of the Today show while speaking about how the relationship began. “And it took a long time. We chatted for a long time, and we became close.”

Aniston was previously married to Brad Pitt from 2000 to 2005 and Justin Theroux from 2015 to 2018. For his part, Curtis wed Rachel Napolitano in 2003 before later going their separate ways. The pair welcomed son Aidan during their marriage.

#3518. Country Singers Name the Musicians They're Most Thankful for This Thanksgiving

Country music is so much more than an industry — it’s a community filled with supporters and cheerleaders.

Need proof? Just look what happened when Us decided to celebrate Thanksgiving by asking artists to share a fellow musician they are grateful for this holiday season.

Time and time again, country singers shared stories of their peers who have offered encouragement, inspiration and friendship in times when it mattered most.

9-1-1: Nashville star LeAnn Rimes will never forget the opportunity she got to learn from Reba McEntire during a Dr. Pepper commercial.

As for Lady A’s Dave Haywood, he continues to look up to Tim McGraw for hitting all the right notes when it comes to “work-life balance.”

Keep reading to see who your favorite country singers are grateful for this Turkey Day:

I’m thankful for Dolly [Parton]. I am thankful for the light she shined on this world, for all the goodness, for her heart. There will never be anyone like Dolly, and I think she showed us what real heart looks like, and she radiated goodness. I just think we could all learn a thing or two from Dolly. I’m just grateful that we got to have her in all of our lives in this lifetime, and I’m grateful that I got to have the time with her that I did, and she was impactful and inspiring to me as not just an artist, but just as a woman in this world. And I always, like everyone else, I always think, “What would Dolly do?” And she would always meet everything and everyone with kindness.

I’m thankful for my buddy, Thomas Rhett. I’ve known Thomas for a long time now, and I have always been a fan of the way he has approached music and his career while keeping his family first; I’ve always respected that. He’s been a role model to me not just in music, but in life. I love him to death and I’m proud to call him a friend.

I would absolutely say Willie Nelson. He has had such a huge influence on me, being from Austin, that I just released a Willie Nelson tribute album. He is a true one of one, a legend, an amazing songwriter, and being on stage with him a few times has been a highlight of my career so far.

I’d have to say Carrie Underwood! I remember early on, when I first got to Nashville, we swapped numbers, and I ended up calling her from the side of the road one day just to ask for advice. She was so gracious with her time and encouragement. She’s continued to be such a kind, steady source of encouragement over the years, even from afar. This industry can be a lot to navigate, especially when you’re young and figuring things out, so I’ve always been really grateful for the kindness she’s shown me. I grew up listening to her music and have looked up to her for a long time, so it’s been really special to experience that same kindness from her personally.

I would say Reba. She is one of the sweetest people I’ve ever known, and in my early, early years — and still to this day — if I see her, she’s just incredibly kind and supportive. I would definitely have to say she kind of tops my list. We did a Dr. Pepper commercial together in my early 2000s and she has always been someone who uplifts everyone around her, including myself. I just love her to death. I can’t say enough good things about her.

I’ve always looked up to Hilary Duff, and she was actually my very first concert! Even though she grew up in the spotlight as a child star, she has always kept a strong head on her shoulders and remained true to herself. I love her message of ‘strong, not skinny’ and the way she continues to promote confidence, self-love and a healthy perspective on body image.

I’m thankful for Stevie Nicks. I’ve always been drawn to women who create an entire world around their music, and Stevie is the ultimate example. Her songs are romantic, haunting, feminine and fierce all at once. What inspires me most at this chapter in my life is how unapologetically herself she has remained. She reminds me that there’s power in your individuality, beauty in your scars and that a woman’s creative spirit only gets more interesting with time.

We are thankful for Jeffrey Steele. There’s something extra special about someone who believed in you back when you were just two guys chasing a dream. Jeffrey has been that person for us, mentoring us through the ups and downs of this industry. We wouldn’t be where we are today without him.

I’m thankful for Tim McGraw and the example he has set for us as a band. His commitment to continuing his legacy through music and touring, while prioritizing his wife and three daughters, is such a beautiful picture of a successful work-life balance. He was actually one of the first to invite us out on a big run, and hopping on his stadium tour this summer was something special. We also were so honored to surprise him during his induction into the Country Music Hall of Fame this year with our take on “Live Like You Were Dying.” He is so passionate about pouring into other artists, and having Tim be a mentor and friend all these years now means so much.

I’m thankful to Vince Gill because he was the very first person who agreed to sing on my very first album, and I hadn’t even met him yet. This act of generosity has taught me to pay it forward with other artists or songwriters. He also told me that using wedges over in ear monitors allowed for the experience of being immersed in music fully. Nashville is the foundation for my songwriting. I’m so deeply grateful for this community.

I’m thankful for Dolly because her talent and legacy have shown me so much. When I was 16, I convinced my parents to move me to Tennessee so I could sing in the country show at Dollywood. I guess you could say I’ve always been grateful for her!

I’m a country singer with California roots, so the west is in my DNA. The Bakersfield sound changed my world. It’s always felt like home to me, and Dwight Yoakam has carried that torch.

Before I had a record deal, Dwight took a chance on me and recorded “Heart Burn” with me. That duet changed my life. Singing with one of my musical heroes was a dream come true, and I’m just as grateful for the friendship that grew out of it with Dwight, his wife Emily, and their son Dalton. Dwight has become a mentor and someone I can call when I’m trying to make sense of this crazy industry. My favorite piece of advice from him is one I still carry with me. He told me, “Go with God.”

Honestly, I’m thankful for Riley Green. There’s been a full-circle story behind our relationship that has shown me grace, humility and what it means to be a true friend. It showed me that a true song wins. Songwriting is King and to treat others the way you wanna be treated.

I’ve known and loved Sheryl Crow’s music since I was a kid. But over the past two years, while writing my last record and going through a deep season of transformation, I found my way back to her albums. Songs I’d known for years took on a completely new meaning. “Strong Enough,” “My Favorite Mistake,” “Maybe Angels,” “The First Cut Is the Deepest”. It felt like I was hearing them for the first time, with enough life behind me to understand them differently.

To me, Sheryl’s music is what embodied art sounds like. There’s something so instinctive about it, like the words and melodies could move straight from whatever she was feeling into the music. You hear the ache, the humor, the desire, the contradictions. It all gets to be there.

In this season of my own life, I’ve been trying to remove as many filters as I can between myself and the audience. That’s made me appreciate the openness in her music even more. It reminds me how powerful a song can be when you let someone close enough to recognize themselves in you. I can get so caught up in finding the right words that sometimes I forget to trust the real ones.

I’m forever grateful for her songs, but just as grateful for her example: the dedication to her craft, the commitment to saying things that matter, and the courage to let the truest parts of herself find a place in the music.

This year, I had the privilege of opening for Kacey Musgraves on her Middle of Nowhere tour. After meeting her and getting to know her, it is clear to me why she is as successful as she is. Not only is she incredibly talented, but she pays attention to details and is very hands-on in everything she does. I witnessed her talking to the lighting director for an hour after her sound check until they got the colors exactly the way she wanted them. She works on all levels of her career. That is how it should be, and that is something I would like to apply to my own career.

I’ll forever be thankful for my friend Keith Urban who was the first artist to take me out on the road as an opener. Watching him thrill crowds every night and run his entire tour like a well-oiled machine was a masterclass on how it’s done.

I’m thankful for Miranda Lambert because she has been supportive of me and my art from the beginning. She sends me long notes after binging my album, making me promise to keep going. She calls when she loves a song. When she asks how I’m doing, she genuinely means it. Miranda is as real and authentic as she is badass.

The fans! The way they show up for me and support me, it really inspires me to keep going and give them everything I have to give. I love The Lefties and I’m so grateful for them!

I’m thankful for Deana Carter. “Strawberry Wine” was one of my favorite songs growing up. It reminded me of my high school sweetheart back in the day. It was just such a nostalgic country song, and it’s still so good even today. I remember when I first kind of started in the country world, I told my producer how much I loved Deana Carter, and she came over and we wrote a song together, and she let me sing “Strawberry Wine” with her, and she didn’t have to do that, and she’s so sweet and such a kind person. I still remember that. I wasn’t known at all in the country world, and she still took the time to sit with me, write a song and let me sing “Strawberry Wine” with her, and it was a memory I’ll always remember. I’ll never forget that.

I’m thankful for Kristian Bush because he’s taught me to be bold, stay true to my roots and always enjoy the ride! A chance meeting at a songwriting festival in Hawaii turned into him producing my very first record, and now I’ve been out on the road opening for Sugarland on my very first arena tour! Getting to learn from one of my childhood heroes every night is a dream come true!

I’m thankful for Rhett Akins because of the support, mentorship, friendship and opportunities he has given me. When I moved to Nashville, I had never done a cowrite in my life. Rhett took a chance on me, and we have now written multiple songs together, and I was also lucky enough to watch him be inducted as a member of the Grand Ole Opry this year.

I’m thankful for Russell Dickerson because he and his wife, Kailey, have been two of my closest friends for almost 20 years. I still can’t believe that writing songs with one of my best friends is a part of my job. We’ve been so lucky to celebrate some pretty big wins together, but getting to live life and raise our kids alongside each other is my favorite part.

#3517. GTA 6 Is A Tragedy Because You Cannot Sit Down And Eat Spaghetti

Everyone, including me, has been making much (rightfully) of how incredible the level of detail in GTA VI is. This game is ridiculous, man! The sheer amount of incidental and specific dialogue, the clothing, the way characters move, the weather, the TV and radio programs, I could go on all day. But there’s a single aspect I’ve found where the level of detail genuinely felt short of what I’d hoped for going in: the food.

You cannot sit down and enjoy a slow, relaxing meal. There is nowhere to order a plate of spaghetti or other food to be eaten explicitly there, in the establishment. There is no cooking. There is only fast food and takeout. And that’s how I know this game is going to be a tragedy.

I love video game food. I love cooking through video game cookbooks, I love beautifully designed and rendered meals within game worlds, and I love creative food crafting systems. So I’m always on the lookout for such things! And in one respect, I actually think GTA VIÂ does food beautifully. It isÂ freaking incredible that you can hold a food and a drink (or two foods, or two drinks) in each hand simultaneously, and swap between consuming each of them at will. Last night, I took Lucia out to a food truck and bought an empanada and a mojito. I had her stand there and take bites of the empanada, and watched with wonder as the empanada disappeared, bite by bite in her hand. (I tried to take a sip of the mojito but accidentally pulled my gun instead and someone called the cops, but I’m sure it would have been equally impressive).

Much has been made of this system, and deservedly. Jason takes bites of apples, and the apples having those bites visible in them until only the core is left! The pair will drink liquids, and you can see the liquids in the containers slowly recede! All of these items have unique models, too: burgers, tacos, croissants, the grilled fish sandwiches made in an early mission that have different levels of char as Jason cooks them…God, it’s incredible! Hats off!

I don’t want anything about that system to change. I love being able to eat handheld foods like this. But what bothers me is that this is…all that Jason and Lucia ever eat.

I complained about this earlier, after a glimpse in the pair’s fridge in an early trailer. Mostly alcohol and protein shakes. Nothing substantial whatsoever to keep two active crime-doers properly fed. But at the time, I thought that was just…their state at that moment in the game. I assumed eventually the pair would end up in a situation where they ate food like normal human beings.

Yet this never happens. I’m in chapter 3, and I’ve consulted with our reviewer who has finished the game, and my understanding is that the pair will never evolve beyond eating on the go. You can’t order a plate of spaghetti or some lo mein and sit comfortably and lazily consume it. The pair never cooks food at home, either as a mechanic or even as a visual suggestion, as their cabinets remain full of nothing but plain bread and cereal and unused pots and pans right up until the end of the game. Every restaurant that looks like it could be a proper sit-down dining establishment is closed and locked to you, and everything that’s open serves like, five things: water, soda, beer, and roughly two handheld food items. And those same 10-20 food items are repeated ad nauesum across all the game’s restaurants, regardless of what’s on the posted menu. In a small handful of establishments, you can sit down to eat those items, but it still doesn’t look like the two are relaxing over a meal. Again, I understood this early in the gameâthe two were broke, Jason was living a bachelor life, and they were on the run. Hell, the motel room in Chapter 2 doesn’t even have its own coffee pot. I get it.

But as the two move to Vice City, build wealth, and start living at a higher standard, I really just thought there’d be some option, somewhere, for one of them to take the other out on a nice dinner date. Maybe just a little cutscene showing a decent plate of food with the two all dolled up. Or perhaps, if that was too risky, the barest suggestion that either of them had ever cooked at home: TV trays, or a dirty pot in the sink, or more than like four spices sitting in the window for some reason. Even like, aÂ discussion about having eaten a meal?

So on one level, I’m disappointed. I love seeing gorgeous food renders in games, and I can only imagine Rockstar’s would be stellar. I think a lot about how the Dragon’s Dogma team bought expensive steak just so they could film themselves cooking it for the game. Or the absurd feasting scenes in Monster Hunter with gorgeous cheese naan. Or even the very simple scenes in the Yakuza games, where you couldn’t see the food, but you could hear the characters discussing how it tasted and what their thoughts were. Impressive as the handheld food is, I’m not really excited at making Jason eat another croissant after I’ve seen the animation a few times. He doesn’t talk about it, it doesn’t seem to do anything for him, he doesn’t even really seem to derive any pleasure from it. Just a health boost maybe.

But even as I’m disappointed by all the storefronts I can’t enter and the menus I read but can never get Jason or Lucia to order from and eat, I’m starting to get what GTA VI is trying to say here. It’s not a budget or a time issue, I know that. If Rockstar devs had wanted to make gorgeous food or record discussions about eating it, they would have. I really do think GTA VI wants to convey in every possible way that this pair will never, ever be safe. They will not be able to slow down or stop or rest for the kind of luxurious meal I want them to have. And that’s luxury not even just in terms of spending lots of money on nice food, but the luxury of time and safety: spending the time to sit, in public, and eat it regardless of where that is. The kind of luxury I feel when my husband and I go to our favorite local Indian joint and, instead of ordering takeout, sit and eat out of the metal trays and sip chai and share naan. If Jason and Lucia sit to eat at all, it will always be in chairs that are easily pushed out, in empty greasy spoons where they can make a quick getaway.

I suspect that wherever the story is going, it is not going to a place where they will be able to comfortably enjoy a slow glass of wine and a fine risotto. It’s not even that it’s an option I can see on the horizon, out of reach due to price or other limitations. It is just, permanently and forever, not for them. Maybe I’ll be proven wrong, and there will be a perfect, peaceful, happy ending where the pair get to live a normal life with their son in a safe place with minimal crime, and where they can go out for a big plate of spaghetti that all three can sit down to enjoy over a wonderful hour of laughter and merriment. Maybe there’s a world where someone could reasonably imagine the three enjoying a multi-hour, homecooked Thanksgiving together. But given all the crime I’ve been doing, somehow I feel that a happy and normal future will, like the many, many restaurants of Leonida, be forever closed to them.

#3516. Kate Middleton Announces Surprise Documentary About Her Cancer Journey

“Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”

But while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton says she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

“Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace says of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”

“It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess says as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that."

I’ve got to be honest. I was NOT dreaming of a white Thanksgiving this week, but that’s what people in many parts of the country got. If you got up this morning wondering how to watch the 100th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade, you may have gotten a rude awakening: It’s not hitting the 2026 TV schedule until Saturday. NBC does have a Turkey Day solution, but honestly, it’s not the one people on the Internet want.

I’m right there with them. It’s still hard to believe that a Nor’easter came in and postponed the parade for the first time in its 100-year history (it has previously been outright canceled), and did so on the actual 100th anniversary. Not even from like, snow. It seems like strong winds made the whole balloon part of the parade impossible. That’s crazy bad luck. However, NBC isn’t sitting on its laurels (and neither is Jimmy Fallon). Here’s what’s happening.

On Thanksgiving, NBC has opted to just throw on last year’s 99th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. NBC may have 99 problems, but no parade ain’t one. It’s not a bad idea really. The big balloons, c-list singers, and jazzy dance breaks are usually something most of us have on in the background anyway on this auspicious day. But social media users have a way better idea.

A slew of social media users think the better play would be to throw on a really old Macy’s Day Parade instead of last year’s. One user on X put it perfectly:

I don't know who needs to hear this, but there are full length recordings of Macy's Thanksgiving Day parades from the '90s, with all the commercials, on YouTube.

They later joked the lineup from 2003 “looked pretty good.” Another user had a specific year request, too, writing:

If they were smart they would air one from, like, 1991 in full.

This isn't the first Macy's Day Parade controversy this season. If you'd rather go the nostalgia play, another X user even noted you can throw one of these old episodes on via YouTube, and I thank this individual for that hot tip.

If you’re missing the Macys Thanksgiving Day Parade this morning you can find recordings of pretty much any year you want on YouTube. We pick a year and watch it every year mainly from the 90s before it turned into some weird rap event. 😂This year we are watching 1994.

It seems as if NBC’s strategy is the network doesn't want viewers to notice the parade is old, but there will be moments anyone actually paying attention to the broadcast should notice. I’m not saying that’s the world’s worst strategy given I already established a lot of us watch this while doing other tasks. Still, I think just going full in and putting on an older broadcast would be really fun, and I think would inspire people to pay closer attention and see what cultural references from the time are mentioned and what’s changed in the decades since.

It’s a great idea, and now I just wish it was happening. Meanwhile, I’m still bummed I’ll have to wait a few more days to see Earl the Squirrel blown up in Epic proportion. Luckily, the Macy’s No-Longer-On-Thanksgiving Day Parade will make its triumphant return to NBC this Saturday. Happy 100th, y’all.
