#3503. MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down

The biggest issue with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge. Anker’s answer in the MagGo 2 Pro is a small fan inside of it. Anker says it keeps the charging surface below 96.8°F, and the fan adjusts its speed based on what’s plugged in and how the charge is progressing. You can switch between Cool and Silent modes if you don’t want to hear it running at all.

The result of having this fan is a Qi2.2 power bank that actually reaches Qi2.2 speeds for a full charge. Anker rates it at 25% on an iPhone 17 Pro in 10 minutes, then to 50% in 25 minutes, which is the kind of speed you’d normally expect from a wired charging session.

The MagGo 2 Pro battery is 10,000mAh, which is enough for a little over one full charge of an iPhone Pro Max and closer to two on a standard iPhone. Size-wise, it has about the same footprint as the iPhone itself and is roughly an ounce lighter than Anker’s standard MagGo. It’s not a slim battery, but for one with a fan, it’s workable in your travel bag, crossbody, etc.

The single USB-C port works both directions at up to 45 watts. If you plug in a 45-watt charger to it, the MagGo 2 Pro can charge from empty to 80% in under an hour. The same port will charge a Mac or an iPad up to 45 watts in a pinch, which is a nice add-on for a MagSafe battery. You are not going to charge up your MacBook Pro from zero to full with it, but it’s a nice way to get a little charge in an emergency at the airport, etc.

One thing to know before you buy: the cable in the box is a 1-foot USB-C-to-USB-C cable, and Anker says that reaching the full 45-watt recharge speed requires a 45-watt-rated cable. So keep that in mind as you pack for a trip.

Anker put a small display on the side that cycles through six screens with a side button: charging wattage, battery percentage, battery health, and temperature. It’s a nice touch to know you are reaching the 25-watt Qi 2.2 speed.

There’s also a built-in stand that adjusts from flat to 80 degrees and folds back into the body when you’re done. You can also quickly turn off charging if you simply want to use it as a stand. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro comes in Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, and Starlight Silver.

Qi2.2 is the Holy Grail of MagSafe chargers, but as I said in the beginning, it’s irrelevant if the heat throttles it. To get full 25-watt MagSafe charging on the go, you’ll likely need something with a fan, unless you’re in colder weather. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro solves that problem with a built-in fan, a handy side display, and a stand.

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is available on Amazon and directly from Anker.

#3502. Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”

When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

Dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

The casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He says to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting new additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

In Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy showed me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she says. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” says Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” says Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the big surprises in the ensemble.”

Taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” says Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” says Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”

Pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” says Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

For Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most important for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

When discussing the best Batman, I'm pretty sure many people will say that Michael Keaton is #1, and I'm not going to disagree. Keaton OWNED that role. That said, is he the most interesting live-action version of the character? I'm going to say no.

In fact, I'm one of those weirdos who will acknowledge that while The Dark Knight is most people's favorite Batman movie, I'm actually of the opinion that Matt Reeves’ The Batman is the best Batman flick. That's all because of Robert Pattinson, who I think is the most fascinating version of Batman yet.

With confirmation that Pattinson is the new James Bond, I have a good feeling that he might also be the most interesting version of 007 yet. Here's why.

While many people will likely say that Keaton is the best Batman, I think it's even more likely that most people will say that Sean Connery is the best Bond. Every subsequent Bond actor has unfortunately been judged against Connery, with many people saying that they liked Daniel Craig's bruiser Bond since he was a callback to the tough guy Bond that Connery represented.

Connery is also the reason why some people disregard Roger Moore's Bond, as some people think he verges too far into the silly territory. Personally, of all men who have played Bond, my favorite is Pierce Brosnan, but I respect those who prefer George Lazenby or Timothy Dalton.

That said, I think Robert Pattinson, who I've already gone on record calling my favorite modern actor, will probably provide the most interesting take on the character yet. When trying to envision him as Bond, I think of his roles in Tenet, The Batman, and Primetime, all rolled into one. I see him being a subtler, quieter Bond than others (maybe closest to Dalton), and I'm looking forward to him creating his own version far removed from anything like Connery. Can you tell that I'm excited?

We've had a James Bond who's been Remington Steele, a James Bond who was in The Golden Compass, a James Bond who was Indiana Jones’ dad, and a James Bond who was in Flash Gordon, but we've never had a James Bond who was ALSO Batman, and I just love that this is now going to be a reality.

I know I'm not the only person who's ever wondered who has the better gadgets, or who would win in a fight, and now that same actor is literally going to be both characters. We're undoubtedly going to have people who are going to argue that Pattinson is a great Batman, but a terrible Bond, or a phenomenal Bond, but a terrible Batman.

Or, you'll have people like me who think that Pattinson is an excellent Batman and (hopefully!) an excellent Bond, and I love that we now live in a timeline where this is a thing. Stupendous!

Honestly, I feel like the search for the next Bond took FOREVER. In fact, just last year, I wrote about how I thought Aaron Pierre would make for a great Bond. Even though it took seemingly a million years to pick another 007, I feel like the final decision came out of nowhere.

Granted, Pattinson had been in the discussion to play Bond for some time now, but I feel like this reveal came out of the blue (Leave it to me to just learn that Pattinson has been manifesting this role for years).

However, now that Pattinson has been confirmed, I'm actually now EXTREMELY excited for this new Bond movie. So much so that while I wasn't really interested before, I'm now all in for a new Bond film. So, great decision! Robert Pattinson can do no wrong!

Update, November 23: The Citrus MacBook Neo with 256GB of storage has dropped even further. It’s now $100 off, sitting at $599. This one will probably sell out fast, so don’t wait! The rest of the MacBook Neo lineup is still $50 off.

The most affordable current-generation MacBook you can get under the tree this year just dropped to its best prices in several months with today’s extremely rare early Black Friday deals. Apple’s MacBook Neo lineup is nearly $50 off to deliver one of, if not the most surprising discounts of the 2026 Black Friday season yet.

Amazon has decided to get even more aggressive with its early Black Friday offerings this week with a solid discount on Apple’s 2026 MacBook Neo, right after delivering AirPods Pro 3 down at an impressive $70 off and the best prices ever across the Apple Watch Series 12 lineup.

As part of the giant collection of new deals landing in its Black Friday sale section this week, it has now dropped the 256GB MacBook Neo down to $649.99 shipped, while the elevated 512GB model sporting the Touch ID keyboard down to $749.99 shipped. Both models are available in various color options at the discounted rate.

While we aren’t talking about something like the major $250 price drops live on the M5 MacBook Air lineup right now, this is, after all, the already extremely affordable current-generation MacBook, at least by Apple standards and despite this summer’s price increase.

While there was a time when you could score one of these for less in brand new condition at retail, those days are long gone now with no signs of return. MacBook Neo remains the most affordable way to land your special someone, or yourself, a new current MacBook this holiday, and it is now at the lowest price we have tracked since the price increases in late June.

It is also worth noting that, while they were lower at launch, there were no overly significant deals back then either and it’s not likely they will drop much lower than they are right now. Not much is safe from Black Friday these days, but the MacBook Neo could have been one of only a very small handful of Apple releases that had and still has the potential to dodge the November price slashing.

Today’s surprisingly rare discounts land on the heels of Apple official raising the eduction pricing at the tail end of last month, and the release of “The Dreamer” – Apple’s new 2026 holiday film starring the new Neo.

#3499. Brooke Williamson Previews Her Delicious Thanksgiving Feast With Bobby Flay

Warning: Chef Brooke Williamson is about to have you gobbling for more as she previews her delicious Thanksgiving feast with boyfriend Bobby Flay.

“This year, I said I wanted to make the turkey, which is not always the case,” Williamson, 48, exclusively shared with Us while discussing her recent partnership with luxury appliance brand Thermador. “We’re doing an Italian theme this year, and Bobby always does a themed Thanksgiving. Last year, we did Southeast Asian Thanksgiving, and everything had Southeast Asian flavors.”

She continued, “I think that having a theme makes it kind of creative and fun, and turns those traditional dishes into something slightly more unexpected.”

According to Williamson, Flay, 61, loves mashed potatoes while she savors stuffing and makes sure the traditional dish is on the table in November.

“I think we’re both really flexible,” she said. “But if I want to make a squash dish, then I do feel like some greens and some vegetables are necessary. Bobby’s more of a starch and protein kind of person, so I will probably add a couple of extra veggies to the table.”

While Williamson joked that her boyfriend wakes up hungry every day, Thanksgiving is extra special for the pair as they both love food and creating special memories in the kitchen.

“Thanksgiving is the ultimate sort of fall, winter holiday in the sense that it’s all about the food. It’s about the family, but there’s less pressure than, like, say, Christmas or Hanukkah with gifts,” she said. “It’s about the food. It’s about the community.”

In between cooking and eating, Williamson tries her best to make time to explore the latest and greatest in kitchen gadgets and appliances.

While visiting Thermador’s showroom in Irvine, California, this month, Williamson was able to check out the brand’s latest innovations, including its next-generation freedom columns refrigeration collection.

“They’re very innovative in the way that they consider elevating your kitchen experience,” Williamson told Us about Thermador. “[This showroom] really showcases the best of these brands and what Thermador has to offer. … I get to cook on some beautiful ranges and out of some beautiful refrigerators that are all state-of-the- art.”

Discovering new flavors, products and innovations are just some of the many reasons why Williamson is so grateful to have the life she has as a chef and best-selling author.

“I think a lot of it is fresh and unexpected in the best way,” she said about her life today. “My life looks very different than it did a few years ago. But then again, it looks different every year. That’s the funny thing about the restaurant industry is that any day moving forward is unexpected. So this is just sort of an amplified version of unexpected every day, and it’s exciting, and it’s fun, and it’s full of joy.”

#3498. Gordon Ramsay’s Daughter Holly Welcomes 1st Baby With Her Husband

Gordon Ramsay is officially a grandpa after his daughter Holly Ramsay-Peaty gave birth to her first baby.

“Daphne June Ramsay-Peaty, Welcome to the World 🩷 25/11/2026 🤍⭐️,” Holly, 26, wrote via Instagram on Thursday, November 26. “You’ll forever be our beautiful baby girl and George’s baby sister. Thank you to all the Doctors, Nurses and Midwives who made sure we were safe, healthy and happy — we will forever be grateful 🤍.”

Gordon, 60, later commented, “Welcome Miss Daphne, congratulations to Adam & Holly wow wow wow 🤩 ❤️❤️❤️ @hollyramsaypeaty @adamramsaypeaty.”

“Baby Ramsay-Peaty coming December 2026 🐣,” she wrote via Instagram in a joint post with her husband, Adam Ramsay-Peaty. “We can’t wait to meet our baby girl.”

Gordon subsequently shared his excitement in the comments section.

“Congratulations to you both. Sending lots of love, Dad ❤️,” he replied at the time. “I’m going to be a very over excited grandad, especially this Christmas.”

Holly is one of Gordon’s six children with his wife, Tana Ramsay. (In addition to Holly, Gordon and Tana, 52, share daughters Megan and Matilda as well as sons, Jack, Oscar and Jesse.)

The influencer married Olympic swimmer Adam in December 2025 after four years together, where Gordon walked her down the aisle at England’s Bath Abbey.

“I’m truly so lucky being able to walk this beautiful bride down the aisle and gaining an incredible son-in-law @adam_peaty!” Gordon wrote via Instagram after the couple’s nuptials. “I love you so much @hollyramsayy and couldn’t be a prouder dad.”

In addition to his ceremony duties, Gordon delivered an emotional speech during the reception.

“It’s tough, honestly. Being the dad with three daughters, you dream of that moment, and that moment arrives, and you’re just like a hot mess,” the celebrity chef joked on the U.K.’s This Morning in January. “But the speech was perfect, it went well. … You’ve got to be warm, emotional. It’s a tough gig.”

Holly and Adam have been together since 2021 before Adam popped the question to Holly in 2024.

“I am marrying my best friend. I truly cannot put into words how I am feeling right now,” Holly captioned Instagram photos. “I still [remember] how big my smile was the morning I got home from my first date with you. “Thank you for letting the little girl inside of me feel loved, seen and happier than ever.”

She added at the time, “I love you, and I cannot wait to be your wife. I promise to always be there with you and George, I’m so [grateful] to be in his life and I cannot wait for more. Everything is better with you. Everything has been better since you. Here’s to forever.”

Adam and Holly’s new arrival is the pro athlete’s second child. He previously welcomed son George with a past partner in 2020.

“I knew everything was going to change from there, but it’s been amazing,” Adam told the BBC in June 2020 months after becoming a first-time dad. “Everyone’s thinking it was an accident but that’s not the case. It’s one of the most beautiful things you can do together and we’ve already sorted the nursery.”

The next year, Peaty told The Independent that fatherhood is “the most rewarding and brilliant thing” that he’s experienced.

“I make decisions now based on how he’s going to perceive it [and] what matters in the long-term for him,” he told the British newspaper in 2021. “It’s less self and more him.”

#3497. Decoding Kate Middleton’s “Tourdrobe” for Her Trip to India

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a new confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

The dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

Wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

“It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley says. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's a very exciting time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe! We're just weeks away from the upcoming Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday hitting theaters, which features a thrilling crossover with four teams of superheroes. That includes the Avengers and the OG stars of the X-Men movies teaming up for the first time on the big screen. Studio boss Kevin Feige recently referenced comments Hugh Jackman made back in the day about this long-awaited moment, and we tracked down the interview.

For years it seemed like seeing the X-Men and Avengers together was a pipe dream, but Disney's acquisition of 20th Century Fox opened the door for it to finally happen. It turns out that long before joining the MCU in Deadpool & Wolverine, Hugh Jackman had hoped to see these teams together on the big screen. Let's break it all down.

Press for the next Avengers movie is underway, with the final Doomsday trailer arriving just days ago. During a recent interview with Empire, Kevin Feige spoke about bringing the X-Men and the Avengers (plus the New Avengers and Fantastic Four) together for the highly anticipated blockbuster. He referenced the Greatest Showman actor by saying:

You see interviews of Hugh Jackman 15, 20 years ago saying, ‘People say it’s impossible, but maybe someday the X-Men and the Avengers can all get together.' It just felt right. It just felt like the fun way to culminate a quarter-century of storytelling.

He's not wrong. The MCU has been going strong since back in 2008, but for years it was noticeably missing beloved Marvel characters like Spider-Man, the Fantastic Four, and the X-Men. The latter had its own series of live-action movies for 19 years, which took place separate from Marvel's shared universe. Those worlds are finally colliding in Avengers: Doomsday, to the joy of fans who have been following the respective properties for well over two decades.

Of course, we had to track down the comments from Jackman that Kevin Feige was referencing to the outlet. They actually date back in 2013.

Hugh Jackman spoke about wanting to see this crossover over a decade ago (2013 to be exact), while promoting his spinoff The Wolverine in an interview with Collider (via YouTube). While Marvel characters were spread across three different studios, the Oscar-nominated actor said the following:

I believe, maybe I'm optimistic, I understand the Marvel has The Avengers, they have a lot of big things going on. But at some point, I just find it almost impossible to believe there's not a way to bring Iron Man and all the Avengers characters to Wolverine, the X-Men characters, Spider-Man and somehow get them in together.

Turns out, he was right on the money. Of course, it took some extenuating circumstances to allow for this crossover to finally happen. Namely, Disney acquiring Fox, as well as the studio forming a joint custody agreement with Sony regarding Tom Holland's Spider-Man. It might have taken an additional 10 years, but we're finally getting the chance to see the Avengers and X-Men on the silver screen together this December.

In the same interview, Jackman addressed the legal headache involved in the possible crossover.

I don't see the impediment. I'm like 'OK, you've got three studios. Just split it three ways in terms of costs. And Happy Days, it's all coming together.

Doomsday has clearly been a long time coming, which should presumably result in massive box office numbers and (hopefully) positive word of mouth. We'll have to see how it all shakes out, but the hype surrounding the project is VERY high. Unfortunately, Jackman wasn't included in the Doomsday cast announcement. Also--Kevin Feige teased more surprise characters being included, and maybe he'll even surprise us and pop up in The Russo Brothers' movie. Fingers crossed for some unexpected moments.

Our answers will come when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. For now, the Avengers and X-Men movies are all streaming over on Disney+.

#3494. Apple Watch SE 3 vs Series 12: Which should you buy this holiday season?

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple Watch is always a popular gift. Apple’s lineup includes the affordable Apple Watch SE 3 and the more advanced Apple Watch Series 12.

Here’s how those two Apple Watch models stack up…

The Apple Watch SE 3 is the most affordable way to enter the Apple Watch ecosystem. It got a big update last year, adding a variety of new higher-end Apple Watch features. It now offers an Always-On display, sleep apnea notifications, temperature sensing, interactive wrist flick and double tap gestures, and more.

The Apple Watch SE 3 offers 18 hours of battery life, though you can stretch that to 32 hours in Low Power Mode. It supports fast charging, going from 0-80% in 45 minutes.

Even though it hasn’t been updated in a year, the Apple Watch SE 3 is a very compelling option, especially for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem. It’s pretty fantastic that you can get an Apple Watch with key display and health-monitoring features for under $200.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is Apple’s newest smartwatch, and it’s a big update over its predecessor. This year, Apple doubled down on the health and fitness capabilities of Apple Watch with an all-new Health Sensing System.

Apple touts that the Apple Watch Series 12 delivers “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” In fact, the company conducted a study of more than 1,000 participants that found the Series 12 “achieved statistically better overall accuracy than every competing wearable it tested across workouts and daily activities.”

With the new system, Apple Watch Series 12 captures your heart rate every five seconds. Previous Apple Watch models, including the Apple Watch SE 3, take measurements every five minutes. The new Health Sensing System also enables a new readiness score feature, which factors in your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score.

As I wrote in my review, the Apple Watch Series 12 brings some of the biggest improvements to Apple Watch health tracking in years. The new sensing system unlocks a trove of new data along with better accuracy.

The Apple Watch lineup is incredibly strong right now. Whether you’re deciding between the SE 3 and Series 12, both offer great health tracking, battery life, and connectivity. The Apple Watch SE 3 is an excellent choice for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem.

The Apple Watch Series 12, however, is the best Apple Watch for most people. There are major improvements to the health tracking capabilities, offering meaningful steps forward in what the Apple Watch can tell you about yourself. In the two months I’ve had mine, I’ve come to appreciate the more frequent heart rate measurement and readiness score.

What do you think of the current Apple Watch lineup? Are you shopping for one this holiday season? Let us know down in the comments.

I watched my first season of Dancing with the Stars this year, and the journey has definitely been a doozy. After tuning in to the competition show on ABC, I was shaken up by the twists and turns that came, including the power of the fan vote that resulted in both Jenna Dewan and Harry Shum Jr. being eliminated ahead of the finale. It turns out that finalist Connor Wood joked about being portrayed as a villain prior to Ezra Frech's historic win.

There was a ton of discourse about DWTS during its last few episodes, with pro Sharna Burgess slamming how fan votes factor in. Plenty of folks online were mad about Wood staying on, while (what many felt were) superior dancers like Harry and Jenna got eliminated. During an interview with THR prior to the finale, Connor spoke about the fan perception of him, offering:

The rest of the internet, totally different story right now. We’ve gotten to a point where I have become a bit of a villain for some people.

Obviously, Connor didn't do anything actually villainous, but his getting through to the Dancing with the Stars finale was a shock for many viewers out there, especially when you compared his performances to those of other contestants. His placement seemed to be entirely due to fan votes, since Wood had the lowest scores in the final weeks of the show. Some fans were worried about whether or not underdog Tatyana Ali would stay in the competition, which ended up resulting in Connor becoming the "villain" of the seasons.

Clearly, the fan vote on Dancing with the Stars is important, but it can also seemingly create more division and drama for those watching the acclaimed reality TV series. Later in the same interview, Wood spoke more about this perception as a contestant, offering:

I think that they think that I personally voted their favorite off, and it’s like — I’m aware of my level of dance skill. I have nothing to do with me staying here. That’s just been just the dark side of making it as far as we made it. My understanding is that the more that people go home, the more the fans of those people will go to someone else’s page and villainize those people. That’s sad, and it’s just a testament to how invested people are in this show.

In the end, Connor would end up in third place on Dancing with the Stars Season 35, beating fellow finalists Maura Higgins and Tatyana Ali. I can only imagine how his "villain" persona might have been amplified if he managed to place even better... especially if he ended up beating Ezra as the winner taking home the Mirrorball trophy this season.

Ultimately the final two pairs of the season were Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, as well as Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach. The latter would end up going home with the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, following a viral final performance where the paralympic athlete's prosthetic leg came off mid-performance. It was a truly epic moment, especially when he managed to overcome it and finish the final dance with his partner.

I thought Ezra was deserving of a win before this final dance, but after seeing the way he overcame and finished the performance, the idea of Connor somehow beating both him and Amber was cringeworthy. In the end that didn't happen, and hopefully Wood can shake off his villain status as more time passes.

Dancing with the Stars is streaming in its entirety for those with a Disney+ subscription as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see what drama comes with the next season of the wildly popular series.

#3492. Brooke Hogan Reflects on Grief Before Thanksgiving Without Dad Hulk Hogan

The Thanksgiving holiday is allowing Brooke Hogan to reflect on the loss of her father, wrestling icon Hulk Hogan.

“I’ve realized that so much of my grief exists in what we will miss together, rather than even what we’ve lost…,” Brooke, 38, wrote via Instagram on Wednesday, November 25. “It’s a strange thing. Nostalgia in reverse. Longing for moments somewhere in the future that feel almost as familiar as memories.”

The founder of BB Designs by Brooke continued, “I miss him in the thought of him falling asleep on my couch, after too much pecan pie, surrounded by the beautiful little family that is an extension of his own. I imagine the evolution of our relationship as I grow older.”

Hulk died in July 2025 at the age of 71. His cause of death was acute myocardial infarction, most commonly known as a heart attack, according to documents obtained by Us.

Although her relationship with Hulk was complicated, Brooke — who shared a throwback photo with her father for her latest post — has been open about her grieving journey and processing different emotions.

“Sometimes the circumstances surrounding a relationship don’t accurately reflect the love that exists within it,” she wrote. “Life and dishonest influence can create distance between two hearts that were never meant to be far apart. I’ll die on that hill. No daughter doesn’t want her daddy.”

“How strange it is to miss someone in a place you’ve yet to visit, at an age you’ve yet to reach, in a moment that’s still somewhere in your future,” she added.

Married to Steven Oleksy, Brooke has two children and currently lives in Florida. She continues to have a fractured relationship with her mom, Linda, 67, and brother, Nick, 36.

“Grief stretches in both directions. It lives in the memories behind you, but also in the life unfolding ahead of you,” Brooke wrote in her latest post. “There’s an entirely different dimension of grief that exists within the beauty of living. The more life there is to celebrate, the more places there are to miss someone.”

While Brooke acknowledged that she has “so much life ahead of me,” it could be why she feels her dad’s absence “so deeply.”

“I’ll miss him in chapters of my life that haven’t even been written yet,” she said. “It’s a longing born entirely out of so much love with nowhere to go. It’s nostalgia in reverse. Being homesick for a future with someone you needed and loved the most.”

#3491. Prince William Reportedly Wants to Strip Prince Harry of His Titles

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”

#3490. Jana Kramer Opens Up About the Pain of Splitting the Holidays After Divorce

Jana Kramer is reminding divorced parents that it’s OK to feel a variety of emotions as they navigate the holidays with or without their kids.

“I think it’s hard because no matter what, it’s not normal for a mom to wake up on Christmas and not have their kids,” Kramer, 42, exclusively shared with Us before the release of her new Lifetime holiday movie, Love on the Christmas List. “This is the year that I don’t get to see my kids on Christmas morning, and I don’t know which is worse. I don’t know whether it’s worse to not have them in the morning or to say bye to them on Christmas Day.”

Kramer shares daughter Jolie, 10, and son Jace, 7, with ex-husband Mike Caussin. She also welcomed son Roman in November 2023 with husband Allan Russell.

“Last year was the first year that I didn’t have a full, complete meltdown. I just kind of had a little cry,” Kramer continued. “I don’t beat myself up for that anymore because I just think about how it’s not supposed to be a normal thing. I’m a mom who wants her kids every day, and I want to wake up to them running down the stairs on Christmas morning. And this year, I don’t get that.”

The former One Tree Hill actress finds comfort in knowing her two oldest kids have a nice time at Caussin’s house. As many parents can relate to, however, Kramer wishes her time wasn’t cut short.

“I do know that they’re having a beautiful morning at their dad’s, and I’ll be ready to open the door for them and have a great rest of the day with them at noon on,” she said. “But I think for any divorced parent that splits on Christmas Day, you dread the morning of not having them, or you dread the noon on Christmas Day having to say goodbye. And to this day, I don’t know which one’s worse.”

Instead of “doomsdaying it,” Kramer has vowed to make the most of the time she does have with her kids. She’s also filled with gratitude for the healthy relationship she has with Caussin, 39, after their public divorce in 2021.

“I think it’s progress on both or all of our ends, you know,” she said. “But you just want your kids to be happy, and you know that they are. That’s the win right there.”

Before Santa arrives for Christmas, Kramer is celebrating Thanksgiving with plenty of food, family and gratitude.

This holiday season, the actress stars in a new Lifetime movie Love on the Christmas List, which is part of It’s a Wonderful Lifetime.

“I would say this is very similar to all the moms that are on the hunt for the best toy for their kids,” Kramer teased about the film. “For this movie, it’s about whether you do what you need to do, whether it’s for your job or for your child, and in the middle of that, you might find a little romance along the way.”

That love interest may just be actor Ignacyo Matynia, who plays a widowed dad also on a quest to find a special gift for his daughter.

“He’s wonderful. He’s great,” Kramer said of her costar. “I’ve never met him before, but he’s such a good actor. We had a lot of fun together.”

With the holiday movie season officially underway, the host of iHeartRadio’s “Whine Down” podcast is grateful that her movies are part of so many family celebrations. She’s also happy to be in a place to experience the magic all around her.

“I think for a long time, I’ve felt unsteady and just like an anxious heart, and I just feel like my children are happy and healthy right now,” she told Us. “I’m healthy, I’m happy. I’ve got a beautiful little family, and I’m really grateful for that because I know that there are a lot of people going through a lot of things, and whether it’s with health or sad hearts, and I just feel for the first time, I feel a very peaceful heart, and that makes me happy.”

Love on the Christmas List premieres on Lifetime Saturday, December 19, at 8 p.m. ET.

#3489. Anthropic launches new Claude Ship feature for builders

Anthropic is launching a new tool for builders called Claude Ship. The new AI feature allows Claude to “review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows.”

Claude Ship is a new product created especially for builders who code with agents. The idea is to make handling pull requests as automated as agentic coding.

“That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic says. “It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what’s ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”

Claude Ship is comprised of three agents: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals.

“Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually,” Anthropic says.

“Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code,” Anthropic says.

You can learn much more about Claude Ship here. Additional documentation can be found here.

#3488. The Return of Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow’s Twisted ‘Hunting Wives’ Love Story

In 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

“I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”

“I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” says showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”

The result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.)

Hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter says, “and eventually seduced.”

Cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she says, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”

Cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

“The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter says, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”

The twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a New York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

Cutter says she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain plan of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”

The second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

“Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter says, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”

#3487. John Mulaney Had To Cut A Segment From His Stand-Up Special After Fast Food Joke Went VERY Wrong

A simple question about a fast-food restaurant can completely derail a comedian's plans.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

With plenty of comedy on the 2026 Netflix streaming schedule, I've always appreciated how John Mulaney can take something ordinary and turn it into an absurdly funny story. Whether he's talking about taking his Korean in-laws to CVS, his children saying scary things, or any number of his hilarious stand-up jokes, his delivery makes even the most ridiculous observations sound perfectly reasonable. Although apparently, one fast-food joke didn't survive the trip from the comedy club to one of his specials, and the reason is pretty hilarious.

The story comes courtesy of filmmaker Cairo Smith, who shared an anecdote on X about attending an early test performance of one of Mulaney's stand-up specials. According to Smith, the comedian had been working on a bit about Yoshinoya Beef Bowl, the Japanese fast-food chain known for its rice bowls. Smith writes in his post, as you can see below, that when the comedian asked audiences who'd been to the establishment, a shocking number had, derailing the entire premise.

One time I went to see an early test performance of a John Mulaney special at a comedy club in LA. And he had a joke about Yoshinoya beef bowl where the joke was that nobody goes there. So he asked the audience, like, who here has actually been to Yoshinoya Beef Bowl? And like a shocking amount of people raised their hands and cheered, like so many that he didn't even know how to continue the bit and just moved on. And then when the special came out, pretty much everything was the same but the Yoshinoya beef bowl bit was gone. And now for some reason that's one of the only John Mulaney bits I can remember.November 24, 2026

According to Smith, the response left Mulaney unsure how to continue, so he simply moved on to his next bit. I have to assume that's not how the comedian was expecting things to god own.

When the finished special eventually premiered, Smith noticed that the Yoshinoya material had disappeared, even though it was the only bit of material they could remember. Considering how many great John Mulaney comedy specials we've gotten over the years, I can't help wondering how many other jokes disappeared during those early performances.

I think the audience unintentionally created a funnier moment than whatever Mulaney originally had planned. There's something wonderful about a comedian confidently walking into a punchline only to discover that everybody in the room has apparently been eating at the restaurant he's mocking. And it seems Mulaney remembers the experience.

Responding to the story on X, Mulaney acknowledged the memory and revealed that he'd encountered a similar problem while testing a recent joke, writing:

l remember this well. The same thing happened in September with a bit I tried about Orange Julius.

I'd love to know exactly what he was planning to say about Orange Julius, because that's another restaurant chain that feels tailor-made for a Mulaney routine. The Yoshinoya detail actually sent me down a bit of a rabbit hole because this isn't the first time the restaurant has figured into one of Mulaney's jokes.

Fans of Saturday Night Live might remember Bill Hader's hilarious return as Stefon in 2018, during which Mulaney appeared as the character's attorney, Shy. At one point, he leaned over to whisper something into Hader's ear. Whatever he said caused Hader to completely lose his composure. Of course, Hader has a long history of losing it during Stefon appearances, and his inability to keep a straight face has produced some of SNL's funniest unplanned moments.

During a subsequent appearance on Late Night With Seth Meyers, Hader revealed that Mulaney had whispered a completely unexpected line about his girlfriend working at Yoshinoya Beef Bowl. It's such an oddly specific thing to say that I can understand why Hader couldn't keep a straight face. Mulaney has a knack for finding humor in names and places that most of us probably wouldn't think twice about.

Mulaney has certainly had plenty of success with the jokes that survived that process. Between his stand-up specials, his work on SNL and his surprisingly personal Netflix series Everybody's Live With John Mulaney, he's established himself as one of the most recognizable comedians working today.

Still, I have to admit that I'd happily watch an entire special made up of the jokes that didn't make the final cut. Especially if they're accompanied by stories about exactly how they fell apart. But for now, I'll happily revisit his prior specials and Everybody's Live with my Netflix subscription.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

#3486. Lego’s First Marvel Rivals Set Is A 495-Piece Tribute To The Game’s Most Adorable Terror

Next month marks the second anniversary of Marvel Rivals, and to celebrate, a new Lego set is on the way that lets you build the game's unofficial mascot, Jeff the Land Shark. While we regularly see Lego Marvel sets roll out, this is the first-ever Marvel Rivals kit, and it'll go on sale starting January 1, 2027, priced at $50. GameSpot can also exclusively reveal the first images of Jeff below, showing the completed build alongside his box art.

See at The Lego Store

The 495-piece set captures the adorable strategist in all his glory, including his big eyes, toothy smile, huge tongue, and even his collar. This won't be a static figure either: once fully assembled, Jeff has a movable head, legs, tail, and fins that let builders recreate his joyful trot, swimming, and battle poses. For added touches, his collar includes his signature name tag, his tongue can be removed to close his mouth, and his fin can be detached so builders can replicate Jeff's Hide-and-Seek movement ability from the game.

"Jeff brings together everything players love about a breakout gaming character: an unforgettable silhouette, a personality you understand instantly, and the ability to turn any match into a story," Lego Marvel design lead Jesper C. Nielsen said in a press release. "We wanted this Lego model to capture both sides of him, from the lovable companion fans want beside their screen to the unpredictable strategist they meet in battle."

Meanwhile, Jeff and the rest of the Marvel Rivals roster are preparing to cap off an entire year of Avengers-centric events that have been building up to the game's big Avengers: Doomsday tie-in. Season 11.5 kicks off on December 11. Nightcrawler was recently added to the game, bringing mutant energy, swords, and teleportation strategies, and he'll soon be followed by Marvel's unique take on Dracula, who has spent the last few months hibernating and healing for the battles ahead.
